fangshan.hook: Four gates, one park: Stone Flower Cave, Zhoukoudian, Shidu, Baishi Mountain — northern valley karst on Wumishan dolostone, not a Guilin fenglin plain.
fangshan.formation_short: Fangshan UNESCO Global Geopark sits on North China carbonate, chiefly Mesoproterozoic Wumishan tidal dolostone (~1.4 Ga) with stromatolites. Dolostone fizzes less than limestone, so northern caves are smaller and stone flowers denser. Shidu is a valley cut by the Juma River. Zhoukoudian caves hold Pleistocene fill. Baishi Mountain is marble. This is northern valley and cave karst, not tropical fenglin.
fangshan.evolution_sequence: Tidal dolostone -> Yanshan fold-and-thrust -> valley karst and caves
fangshan.what_you_see_today: Near-horizontal beds in a river bend at Shidu; stone flowers in a slow cave; a marble ridge at Baishi.
observation_tips: Dolostone: weak fizz.
Stromatolites on fresh faces look like sliced blankets.
Zhoukoudian is a cave-fill section, not a souvenir bone shop.

shihuadong.what_you_see_today: Name dolostone as the wall. Do not touch speleothems. Commercial lights are not the process.

jixian.hook: North China's deep-time ruler. A Mesoproterozoic sea stacked on the hills of Jizhou.
jixian.formation_short: The Jixian section is marine carbonate and clastic rock of the Meso- to Neoproterozoic, rich in stromatolites. The Yanliao sag kept a continuous record; later uplift cut a textbook section. Walk the groups in order. This is a stratigraphic ruler, not a karst scenic mountain and not the granite of nearby Panshan.
jixian.evolution_sequence: Rift clastics -> carbonate platform -> uplift to a type section
jixian.what_you_see_today: Wumishan stromatolites like sliced cabbage. Convex-up marks the top. Do not chisel.
observation_tips: Stromatolite convex-up tells you the way up.
Songshan shows unconformities; Jixian unfolds the Proterozoic itself.

changbaishan.geologic_age_text: Age as listed on the Chinese park page.
changbaishan.hook: A trachyte–pantellerite compound volcano. Tianchi is a water-filled caldera from the ~946 CE millennium eruption, not a meteor crater.
changbaishan.formation_short: Changbaishan UNESCO Global Geopark is an intraplate volcano on the China–Korea border, not an island arc, not a meteorite. Shield: basalt. Cone: trachyte. Caldera: pantellerite (alkaline rhyolite) and pumice that floats. The millennium eruption ~946 CE was Plinian. Jingpohu is a basalt dam on the Mudanjiang; Wudalianchi is potassic scoria — different magma. Tianchi is not a tiankeng and not an impact. Pumice is not granite.
changbaishan.evolution_sequence: Basalt shield → trachyte cone → Plinian eruption → caldera lake
changbaishan.what_you_see_today: A cold lake in a collapsed magma chamber. Grey-white pumice on the slopes is 946 CE, not snow.
observation_tips: Rim rock has vesicles or flow banding, no sedimentary bedding.
Pumice floats.
The waterfall cuts a lava-and-tephra dam, not limestone.
safety_notes: Crater walls and scoria slopes are loose — stay on the path.
Watch for burns at hot springs.
Do not climb crater fences.
changbaishan.legal_notes: Protected geoheritage. Look, photograph, note. Do not hammer, dig, or take rock, mineral or fossil. Prices and hours follow the official listing on the day. This guide does not sell tickets.
corrections: Tianchi is a caldera, not a meteor crater and not a karst tiankeng.
The millennium eruption is about 946 CE, not a sixteenth-century myth.

wudalianchi.hook: In 1719–1721 Laoheishan and Huoshaoshan dammed the Baihe. Five lakes are lava-dam products.
wudalianchi.formation_short: Wudalianchi sits on a deep fault between the Lesser Hinggan and Songliao. Potassic basalt rose along the fault: fourteen cones, old and new. Dark, vesicular, olivine sometimes visible. New scoria is loose; ropey and pressure-ridge crusts record a cooled skin over a still-moving core. Old Pleistocene cones are wooded; the new ones erupted 1719–1721 and dammed five bead lakes. Not a meteor crater, not a Changbaishan caldera, not Jingpohu’s single basalt dam without fresh scoria cones.
wudalianchi.evolution_sequence: Fissure basalt → scoria cones → lava dam → five lakes
wudalianchi.what_you_see_today: Black new lava with little plant cover, wooded old cones, a chain of lakes behind a stone dam.
observation_tips: Count scoria layers in Laoheishan’s inner wall.
Ropey lava is perpendicular to flow.
Stay off unstable dam rock.
safety_notes: Crater walls and scoria slopes are loose — stay on the path.
Watch for burns at hot springs.
Do not climb crater fences.

sheshan.hook: Sheshan is a Late Cretaceous alkaline volcanic remnant in southwest Shanghai — andesitic–trachytic to rhyolitic. An urban geosite, not a national geopark. Shanghai's national geopark is Chongming Island. The church and observatory were built later.
sheshan.formation_short: Sheshan is a rock hill, not dumped fill. The rock is Late Cretaceous alkaline volcanic: andesitic–trachytic to rhyolitic tuff, lava and pyroclastics, pale grey to purple-grey, sometimes with phenocrysts, tuff fragments or flow banding. It belongs to the Zhejiang–Fujian coastal volcanic belt at the Yangtze mouth. Not granite, not a Wudalianchi-style basalt scoria cone, not a maar. West Sheshan is about 100 m, the highest point on Shanghai land. East Sheshan and Tianmashan are the same volcanic hills. Do not cut the rock. Sheshan is an urban geosite. Shanghai's national geopark is Chongming Island.
sheshan.evolution_sequence: Late Cretaceous eruption → isolated volcanic hill → later weathering
sheshan.what_you_see_today: East Sheshan, West Sheshan and the other Songjun nine peaks. West Sheshan is the highest point on Shanghai land. On open paths, name pale massive volcanic rock: phenocrysts, tuff fragments or flow banding. Do not use the church or observatory as the rock cover. Contrast with Chongming sand island: there the sand is still Holocene and unconsolidated; here the rock is Late Cretaceous alkaline volcanic, on the order of seventy million years.
observation_tips: First touch the pale massive volcanic rock and tuff fragments. Pale grey to purple-grey, not a dark fine lava plateau.
The church and observatory are later buildings, not field marks of this rock.
Shanghai's national geopark is on Chongming Island, not at Sheshan.

huangshan.hook: Early Cretaceous granite taken apart by vertical joints and spheroidal weathering. The Guest-Greeting Pine grows in a joint, not in a volcanic neck.
huangshan.formation_short: Huangshan is a granite pluton on the Jiangnan orogen, zircon ages about 125–128 Ma, coarse porphyritic to medium grain. Emplaced kilometres down — not a neck. Front ranges have sparser joints (domes and tors); the back ranges have denser vertical joints (clusters and pillars). Neighbours Jiuhua, Sanqing and Tianzhu share that granite pulse. Unloading joints sit near-horizontal; tectonic joints stand up. Sequence: country rock stripped, joints make pillars, spheroidal weathering rounds edges, ice-margin and streams cut West Sea Canyon. Not sandstone peaks, not karst, not a volcano.
huangshan.evolution_sequence: Pluton → uplift → joints → pillars and tors → canyon widening
huangshan.what_you_see_today: Pines in joints, tors on summits, a joint-walled canyon at West Sea. Coarse quartz and feldspar, no bedding.
observation_tips: Coarse quartz + feldspar on a fresh face.
Tors are weathering rinds.
West Sea walls are nearly parallel — they follow joints.
safety_notes: Joint faces shed blocks.
Do not climb unprotected walls.
Rock is slick in rain.

corrections: Huangshan granite is not a volcanic neck.

zhangjiajie.geologic_age_text: Age as listed on the Chinese park page.
zhangjiajie.hook: A Middle Devonian quartz beach, jointed into a forest of pillars.
zhangjiajie.formation_short: Zhangjiajie sits on the western Yangtze Platform. Middle Devonian shoreface quartz sand became the Yuntaiguan Formation: silica-cemented, thick-bedded, metres to hundreds of metres thick. Mesozoic–Cenozoic uplift lifted the beach above base level. Two near-vertical joint sets, NW and NE, diced the slab. Neighbouring Yellow Dragon Cave is limestone — it does not make the pillars karst. Water cut the joints first; gravity then thinned walls into pillars. You are looking at the pillar-to-remnant stage; Yuanjiajie and Tianzishan still show mesa tops. It is not karst (no fizz) and not Danxia (local rust is iron stain, not a red-bed colour). Field tests: sandy feel, square sections, soft beds recessed after rain.
zhangjiajie.evolution_sequence: Quartz beach → thick sandstone → uplift → joint grid → mesa → wall → pillar forest
zhangjiajie.what_you_see_today: Grey-white sandstone pillars with square sections. Mesa tops survive on Tianzishan and Yuanjiajie. Yellow Dragon Cave is the limestone check inside the park — a different rock.
observation_tips: No acid fizz on the pillars; cave walls do fizz.
Square sections = two vertical joint sets.
Soft interbeds make ledges after rain.
safety_notes: Rockfall in the peak forest — do not climb fences.
Sandstone is slick in rain.
Do not climb unprotected pillars.
zhangjiajie.legal_notes: Protected geoheritage. Look, photograph, note. Do not hammer, dig, or take rock, mineral or fossil. Prices and hours follow the official listing on the day. This guide does not sell tickets.
corrections: Zhangjiajie is a quartz-sandstone peak forest, not karst.
Zhangjiajie is not Danxia. Local rust is iron stain, not a red-bed colour.

danxiashan.formation_short: Danxiashan is the type locality, a Cretaceous–Palaeogene red basin south of the Nanling. Iron oxide is depositional, not paint. Taining and Langshan share the process. Zhangye colourful hills do not. Colour is not enough — you need the joint-and-collapse sequence.

Not three unrelated parks. Not tiankengs. Hainan does have a UNESCO Global Geopark — it is this park’s southern unit. Magma met water to make the maar; fissure eruptions built the scoria. Haikou Volcano and Huguangyan are national parks counted as units, not extra UNESCO parks. The world count stays 51.
leiqiong.evolution_sequence: Rift basalt → maar explosion + scoria cones → lakes and lava tubes
leiqiong.what_you_see_today: A round lake inside a tephra ring at Huguangyan; black scoria at Haikou.
observation_tips: Maar walls are volcaniclastic, no fizz.
Haikou: scoria and ropey lava. Do not freelance lava tubes.

shilin.hook: A Lower Permian sea, stood on end as a forest of stone.
shilin.formation_short: Shilin is Maokou limestone on the southwestern Yangtze Platform: thick, fossiliferous, soluble. Late Permian Emeishan basalt once covered it; Cenozoic laterite buried it again. The stone forest was exhumed, not left naked since the Permian. A vertical joint grid diced the plateau. Xingwen, nearby, took the same beds into caves and tiankengs. Not Danxia, not Zhangjiajie. Fizz on fresh limestone; look for the grid in plan.
shilin.evolution_sequence: Permian limestone → basalt and laterite cover → exhumation → jointed pinnacles
shilin.what_you_see_today: Sword-like pinnacles in a joint grid. Soil and laterite still sit in pockets between them.
observation_tips: Acid fizz on limestone.
Pinnacles follow a joint grid.
This is surface karst; caves and tiankengs are the underground chapter at other parks.
safety_notes: Follow the cave brief; do not leave the group.
Stay out of ungated sinks and streams after heavy rain.
Do not hammer or touch speleothems.

corrections: Shilin is karst on Maokou limestone, not quartz sandstone and not Danxia.

chengjiang.formation_short: Chengjiang is an Early Cambrian sea, not a treasure pit. Yu’anshan Formation (Maotianshan shale) ~518 Ma, thin, dark, flat. Quiet, sometimes anoxic water on the Yangtze Platform preserved arthropods, lobopodians, sponges and chordates as soft-bodied films. World Heritage and IUGS geoheritage. Uplift and differential weathering brought the paper-shale to view. Fossils are state property.
chengjiang.evolution_sequence: Quiet sea → exceptional burial → uplift → protected outcrop and museum
chengjiang.what_you_see_today: Paper shale and museum slabs. The field is a horizon, not a quarry.
observation_tips: Read the museum first.
The bed is millimetres. No splitting for souvenirs.

zhangye.hook: Colourful hills from redox in lacustrine sandstone and mudstone — not Danxiashan-style Danxia.
zhangye.formation_short: Zhangye sits on the north Qilian basin. Cretaceous lake and river mudstone, siltstone and sandstone were stripped by desert wind and cloudbursts into coloured hills. The rock is soft. Reds and yellows are ferric iron; grey-green is a reducing facies — colour locked in at deposition, not painted later. Neighbour Danxiashan has joint-controlled red cliffs and mesas; Kanbula is plateau Danxia; Dunhuang is yardang. None of those sequences live here. Stay with colour banding and grain size, not with a Danxia label sold on a ticket.
zhangye.evolution_sequence: Cretaceous lake beds → Qilian uplift → wind and storm stripping → colourful badlands
zhangye.what_you_see_today: Banded red, yellow and grey-green slopes. Soft rock, no joint-controlled alleyways of the Danxia type locality.
observation_tips: Colour follows beds, not joints.
Soft mudstone recesses; sandstone stands a little proud.

hongkong.hook: When the tide goes out, a hexagonal cooling-joint net appears. Acid rock grows columns too.
hongkong.formation_short: Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark has two limbs: Sai Kung volcanic rock and northeast New Territories sedimentary rock, on the Early Cretaceous volcanic–sedimentary belt of the South China margin. The columns are rhyolitic lava and ignimbrite, not basalt: pale to dark, quartz and feldspar phenocrysts. Joints grew perpendicular to the cooling surface. Coordinates stay in WGS84 on the map — Hong Kong is not offset to GCJ-02. Read the tide.
hongkong.evolution_sequence: Early Cretaceous acid volcanics → cooling joints → marine erosion of the columns
hongkong.what_you_see_today: Hexagonal columns in the intertidal, a joint net when the tide is low.
observation_tips: Tide table first.
Pale phenocrysts — not black basalt.
No GCJ-02 shift on this park.
safety_notes: Read the tide table before going down to the columns. The intertidal can cut you off.
Wave-cut platforms are slick — do not climb the columns or drop off the cliff.
Stay on marked country-park paths. Do not hammer or take rock.
hongkong.legal_notes: Hong Kong is a separate jurisdiction. Mainland China’s Fossil Protection Regulations do not apply as such. Do not hammer, dig, or take specimens. Follow the Country Parks Ordinance and on-site notices.
corrections: Columnar jointing is not a basalt franchise. Acid rock can do this.

zjj-huangshizhai.name: Huangshizhai
zjj-huangshizhai.look_here: The stockade top is flat. Name the platform first, then the cut edges.

wdlc-laohei.name: Laoheishan crater
wdlc-laohei.look_here: Stand on the rim. Count scoria layers on the inner wall. This cone is 1719-1721.

wdlc-shengli.name: Lava tumulus
wdlc-shengli.look_here: Broken pahoehoe crust. Not a quarry dump.

wdlc-sanzuokou.name: Lava-dammed lakes
wdlc-sanzuokou.look_here: Point across the water to the lava dam. The lake is a blocked river, not a crater.

wdlc-rope.name: Ropey lava
wdlc-rope.look_here: Skin cold, interior still flowing. The rope direction is the flow.

fs-shidu.name: Shidu, Juma valley
fs-shidu.look_here: A river gorge in carbonate. Northern karst is a valley, not a fenglin plain.

fs-shihua.name: Stone Flower Cave
fs-shihua.look_here: Stone flags and flowers grew from dripwater. Do not touch.

fs-baishi.name: Baishi Mountain
fs-baishi.look_here: Marble peaks. Contrast with Wumishan dolostone in the cave.

fs-zhoukoudian.name: Zhoukoudian cave
fs-zhoukoudian.look_here: Read the cave-fill beds. Fossils are in the exhibits. Area only.

shd-flowers.name: Stone-flower galleries
shd-flowers.look_here: Stone flowers and flags on Wumishan dolostone. Look, do not touch. Coloured lights are not the process. Northern caves are slow and small — not a Guilin fenglin plain.

shd-wall.name: Wumishan wall bedding
shd-wall.look_here: Mesoproterozoic dolostone bedding at an open gallery. Stromatolite convex-up. Weak fizz compared with limestone.

shd-gate.name: Open cave-mouth floors
shd-gate.look_here: Stacked halls follow joints. Stay with the group. Do not touch speleothems.

sd-wall.name: Juma valley wall
sd-wall.look_here: Near-horizontal Wumishan beds. Fizz means carbonate. Northern valley karst — not Guilin fenglin, not Danxia cliffs.

sd-bend.name: Shidu canyon bend
sd-bend.look_here: A river meander cut into bedrock. 'Ten ferries' is a place name, not ten geologic fords. Name the rock before the bend.

xqs-quarry.name: Quarry-cave wall
xqs-quarry.look_here: A trachyte quarry void. Tool marks, not stalactites, not pahoehoe. Xiqiao is not a limestone cave and not Hawaiian basalt.

xqs-dome.name: Trachyte dome from afar
xqs-dome.look_here: A Cenozoic trachyte dome, not a basaltic scoria cone, not an active volcano, not a Leiqiong maar.

xqs-joint.name: Tabular-joint path
xqs-joint.look_here: Tabular to columnar joints and pale phenocrysts. Name the rock, then see how quarrying opened the joint faces.

lc-section.name: Heimugou loess–palaeosol section
lc-section.look_here: Wind-blown loess with palaeosol bands, vertical joints, carbonate nodules. Not red-bed Danxia. Stay back from the cut after rain.

lc-yuan.name: Loess yuan surface
lc-yuan.look_here: Yuan, liang and mao are wind-blown silt later cut by water. Name the silt first, then the dissection.

lc-gully.name: Gully cut face
lc-gully.look_here: Vertical joints control the gully wall. Mud after rain. Read the section. Do not collect loess.

xx-section.name: Xixian loess section
xx-section.look_here: Quaternary wind-blown loess, vertical joints, carbonate nodules. Not red-bed Danxia. Stay back from the cut.

xx-yuan.name: Yuan–liang–mao from afar
xx-yuan.look_here: Wind stacked the silt; water cut yuan, liang and mao. Name the silt first.

fangshan-shihuadong.name: Stone Flower Cave unit
fangshan-shihuadong.summary: A northern karst cave. Stone flags, draperies and flowers in Wumishan dolostone.

fangshan-zhoukoudian.name: Zhoukoudian unit
fangshan-zhoukoudian.summary: Peking Man site. Cave fill and human evolution — not a place to dig fossils.

fangshan-shidu.name: Shidu unit
fangshan-shidu.summary: A carbonate gorge cut by the Juma River — the valley face of northern karst.

fangshan-baishishan.name: Baishi Mountain unit
fangshan-baishishan.summary: Laiyuan, Hebei. Marble peak forest — a cross-province unit of Fangshan UNESCO Global Geopark.

hk-saikung.name: Sai Kung volcanic unit
hk-saikung.summary: Early Cretaceous acid-rock columnar joints, the IUGS geoheritage site.

hk-ne.name: Northeast New Territories sedimentary unit
hk-ne.summary: Sedimentary coasts, faults and differential erosion.
